title: U.S. House, District 27
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 27th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: Roster from CBS Miami, Local 10 and WLRN post-primary reports: Maria Elvira Salazar (R) vs. Eliott Rodriguez (D). No NPA candidate identified; absence unconfirmed. Sources: https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/2026-florida-primary-district-27-republican-maria-elvira-salazar/ ; https://www.local10.com/news/politics/2026/08/18/florida-primary-coverage-of-us-house-races-for-the-27th-congressional-district/ ; https://www.wlrn.org/government-politics/2026-08-18/ex-tv-anchor-eliott-rodriguez-27-district Florida adopted a new congressional map (passed Apr 29, 2026, signed May 4, 2026) that reworked 21 of 28 districts; county descriptions here reflect post-redistricting reporting where found (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-05-06/breakdown-changes-for-florida-new-congressional-map).

candidates.residence: Coral Gables area, Miami-Dade County (not re-verified)
candidates.background: Maria Elvira Salazar, a former television journalist, has represented the 27th District since January 2021. She is the lead Republican sponsor of the bipartisan Dignity Act immigration bill (H.R. 4393, reintroduced July 2025 with Rep. Veronica Escobar). She won the Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary with 81.3% of the vote over Coral Gables attorney V. Michael Arias (18.7%). In September 2026 she aired a campaign ad saying the administration's immigration enforcement has 'gone too far.'
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Republican primary with 81.3% over V. Michael Arias (18.7%) (CBS Miami; Florida Politics)

candidates.name: Eliott Rodriguez
candidates.occupation: Retired broadcast journalist (former CBS News Miami anchor)
candidates.background: Eliott Rodriguez, 69, is a retired broadcast journalist who anchored at CBS News Miami for 25 years after nearly five decades in journalism; he was born in New York to Cuban immigrant parents. He left the station and announced his candidacy in March 2026, reported raising $312,000 in his first 21 days, and won the Aug. 18 Democratic primary with about 53.5% over former homicide prosecutor Robin Peguero. His campaign centers on affordability, protecting Social Security and Medicare, restoring health-care subsidies, opposing tariffs and opposing the Trump administration's immigration enforcement.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Democratic primary with ~53.5% over Robin Peguero (CBS Miami; WLRN)
